title: Month 20
subtitle: Pretend play is starting, and it is the best language tool you have.

baby.development: Your child is running, can walk up stairs with a hand held, and says around twenty to fifty words. They are starting to pretend, like stirring a pot or putting a toy to bed.

you.body: Your body has been carrying a growing child for twenty months. If something hurts, it is worth a physio visit rather than a wait.
you.mind: Twenty months is when the child's play becomes a window into what they understand. Watching it is more useful than any checklist.

coreActions.title: Play pretend with them, and follow their lead
coreActions.why: Pretend play is where language, memory, and social understanding come together, and it works best when the child is the one deciding.
coreActions.detail: Sit on the floor and copy what they do. If they stir a pot, stir a pot. Add one idea, not five. A box is a car, a spoon is a phone. Do not correct the game, join it.

coreActions.title: Book the two-year visit
coreActions.why: The two-year visit is the second autism screen and the next developmental check, and the good slots go early.
coreActions.detail: The two-year visit usually has no vaccines if the eighteen-month set is complete. The doctor will do a second autism screen and check language, movement, and teeth. Write down the words and the two-word phrases.

coreActions.title: Teach the stairs, and keep the gate
coreActions.why: A child can learn to go down stairs backwards on their tummy long before they can do it on their feet.
coreActions.detail: Practise going down on the tummy, feet first, with you below. Keep the gates at the top and the bottom. A child is not safe on stairs alone until around three.

alsoKnow.title: The second molars are the last teeth
alsoKnow.body: Second molars usually arrive between twenty-three and thirty-three months, and they are the ones that wake a child at night. The full set of baby teeth is complete around three.

alsoKnow.title: Sharing is not a two-year-old skill
alsoKnow.body: A two-year-old is not developmentally able to share. Parallel play, side by side with the same toys, is the goal. Taking turns with a timer works better than asking for a share.

redFlags.text: Choking — cannot breathe, cough, or make a sound
A fever over 100.4°F with unusual sleepiness or a rash
Fast or labored breathing, or a blue tint around the lips
